sections.history: Tiruchengattangudi is an old Shaiva village near Tirumarugal, revered in the seventh-century Tevaram and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams on the southern bank of the Kaveri. Its deepest fame comes from the Pallava age, as the home of Siruthonda Nayanar — identified in tradition with Paranjothi, a commander of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I. The temple of Shiva and the nearby shrine of Vatapi Ganapati together make the village a living memorial to that era of saint and conquest.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian complex with a gopuram, pillared halls and the sanctum of Ganapatheeswarar, with a separate shrine for the goddess Vaata Thirukkuzhal Nayaki. A famed sculptural panel within the temple depicts the story of Siruthonda Nayanar, and the celebrated image of Vatapi Ganapati is enshrined here. The stonework reflects Chola-period building over earlier foundations, and the village retains the atmosphere of a place shaped by a single, powerful legend.
sections.legends: The central story is that of Siruthonda Nayanar and his son Seeralan. A Shaiva ascetic, in truth Shiva himself, came as a guest and asked to be fed the flesh of the family's only son. Siruthonda and his wife, in the extremity of their devotion, consented; and when the meal was prepared the guest revealed himself as the lord, restored the boy to life and raised Siruthonda to the ranks of the Nayanmars. The sthala-purana also tells that Ganesha worshipped Shiva here to atone for slaying the demon Gajamukhasura, and that the lord appeared as a lingam at the spot — the place name recalling the blood-reddened ground of that combat.
sections.festivals: The temple observes the Shaiva festivals and holds the memory of Siruthonda Nayanar in special honour, with observances tied to the saint. Vinayaka Chaturthi is naturally significant given the village's association with Vatapi Ganapati, and the annual festival draws devotees who know the Periyapuranam story and come to stand where it is set.
sections.experience: Tiruchengattangudi is a place where devotion is remembered at its most unflinching. Pilgrims come for darshan of Ganapatheeswarar and of Vatapi Ganapati, and to see the panel of Siruthonda's trial — a story that asks what faith can demand and what grace can restore. The village has the grave, reflective air of a shrine that keeps one of the hardest tales in the Shaiva tradition.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruchengattangudi is near Tirumarugal in Tiruvarur district, roughly 20 km from both Tiruvarur and Nagapattinam; the nearest rail heads are Tiruvarur and Nagapattinam, with local buses and taxis to the village.
